ai.description: *Sepsophis punctatus* reaches 15 cm. It is golden-brown with longitudinal rows of black spots. This limbless skink is distinguished by its wedge-shaped snout and lack of visible limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Sepsophis punctatus* is uniquely identified by its distinct longitudinal rows of dark spots along the body, which contrast with the plain or striped patterns of other Indian skinks.
ai.habitat: *Sepsophis punctatus* inhabits the moist, leaf-littered floors of tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the northern Eastern Ghats at moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: *Sepsophis punctatus* is a secretive, fossorial skink that remains hidden beneath leaf litter and soil, emerging primarily to forage for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sepsophis punctatus* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sepsophis punctatus* is endemic to the Eastern Ghats in the Indian states of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, typically inhabiting moist deciduous forests at low elevations.
